preamble: Backing and rounding the nucleus of the PRICE diphthong /aɪ/ toward [ɒɪ ~ ɔɪ] is a feature of the broad end of the Australian and New Zealand accent continua. Broad Australian English raises and rounds the first element, giving [ɒːe] against General [ɒe] and Cultivated [a̠e], as in price /ˈpɹɒ̈ɪ̯s/ and nice /nɒ̈ɪ̯s/. Broad New Zealand English retracts and rounds it to [ɒɪ], at times raised further to [ɔɪ]. The rounded variants approach CHOICE without merging with it and are socially stigmatised.

examples.note: Wiktionary lists the rounded variant beside /ˈpɹɑ̟ɪ̯s/ for Australian and New Zealand English. In broad accents the first element of PRICE is raised and rounded, giving [ɒːe] (Wells 1982: 597; Harrington, Cox & Evans 1997).
The from forms are the General or Cultivated pronunciation, which keeps the conservative unrounded nucleus.

The first element of /aɪ/ is retracted and rounded in Broad NZE to [ɒɪ], raised further to [ɔɪ]; it approaches CHOICE /oɪ/ without an actual merger, and the rounded variants are stigmatised. The from forms are the Cultivated pronunciation, which keeps the conservative unrounded nucleus.
Broad NZE PRICE and FACE share the offglide [e].
